# P3.7 The SPA check fetches a hashed asset, not only the shell

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | P3 |
| Role | IMPLEMENTATION |
| Level | L1 |
| Contracts | C-ISO@1 |
| Depends | P3.1 |
| Findings | none |
| Confidence | reproduced by the P3.1 implementation review on the reviewer's own bundle (`docs/v2/state/reviews/P3.1-impl.md:46-67`) |

## Objective
`scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.test.sh`'s SPA check can no longer pass on
a bundle that contains no JavaScript, and the assertion that does the work is a
**content type**, not a byte count.

P3.1's Step 3 fixed the check as "`GET /` is 200 with `content-type: text/html`
and a non-empty body … an empty or truncated copy of `web/dist` must fail here
rather than in a person's browser" (`docs/v2/cards/P3.1.md:304-307`). The
implementation review returned **PASS** and found that the check cannot do the
second half of that sentence. All three SPA assertions inspect `GET /` only
(`:429-448`), and `index.html` survives `rm -rf web/dist/assets` intact, so
`spa-status`, `spa-content-type` and `spa-body` **all pass on a bundle with no
script and no fonts in it** (`P3.1-impl.md:46-56`). The review demonstrated it,
judged it major, and carried it forward rather than blocking; P3.1's green does
not close it (`P3.1-impl.md:186-190`).

This card adds the one assertion that was missing. It changes nothing else.

## Fixed decisions
1. **One check, named `spa-asset`, placed immediately after `spa-body`** (so
   between `:448` and `:450`) and before the whisper check. It fetches **the
   one hashed script the served shell actually references** and requires the
   following of that response:
   - the reference is **found**: the `src="…"` attribute is extracted from the
     **served** `GET /` body (the `$ROOT_BODY` the script already captured at
     `:429-430`, not the file on disk, so the shell and the server are proven to
     agree). Exactly one `src="` is expected. **Zero, or more than one, is a
     `FAIL spa-asset` with the count in the detail — never a skip and never a
     pass**, because a check that quietly finds nothing is the defect this card
     exists to remove.
   - `GET <that path>` answers **200**.
   - its `content-type` contains `javascript`.
   - its body length, **counted in bytes**, equals the `bytes` `manifest.json`
     records for that path (Fixed decision 3).
   The failure detail names which of these failed and prints the observed
   status, content type and byte count, so a reviewer reads the reason from the
   row's own output.

   Two things the comparison is **not**, both because the file's own idiom is the
   trap. The length is **bytes the server sent, not characters of a shell
   variable**: the asset body is written to a file in the run folder and measured
   with `wc -c <file>` or `curl -o <file> -w '%{size_download}'`, never with
   `${#VAR}`. Under the run's `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` `${#VAR}` counts characters, and
   on the bundle on disk today the two readings differ — `index-D7iOgJVA.js` is
   169523 bytes and 169480 characters — so mirroring `spa-body`'s
   `${#ROOT_BODY}` (`:444`) would `FAIL spa-asset` on a **perfect** bundle. The
   manifest is read from the bundle under test, keyed on `web/dist` + the served
   path; a path the manifest does not list is `FAIL spa-asset` with the path in
   the detail, which is Stop condition 3's case stated in the check rather than
   only in the stop list.

   **The success path prints the four values too**, as one informational line
   that is **not** prefixed `PASS ` and does not go through `pass()` — e.g.
   `spa-asset /assets/index-D7iOgJVA.js 200 application/javascript 169523`, in
   that order, separated by single spaces. `pass()` prints the name alone
   (`:37-39`) and is not changed, so this is the one extra line the check is
   allowed to print; it exists because the row's acceptance and the return file
   both ask for those four values, and they have to reach the evidence from
   somewhere. One line, only on success, never `FAIL`-prefixed.
2. **`server/src/app.ts` is not changed, and the content-type assertion is what
   carries the check.** This is worth stating plainly because the review
   suggested the static handler would also have to change
   (`P3.1-impl.md:64-67`): it does not, and it must not. The fallback answers a
   missing asset `200 text/html`, and a real one `200 application/javascript`,
   so the content type alone separates a truncated bundle from a good one — the
   control returned 1265 bytes of HTML where a real asset returned 169523 bytes
   of JavaScript. A future implementer who "fixes" the fallback to return
   `404` for unmatched asset paths would change what a reload of a client-side
   route does — that fallback is why `/patients` resolves on a fresh load — and
   it would buy this row nothing it can measure, because the content type
   already discriminates. Do it and it is a Stop condition.
3. **The length assertion is the bundle's own record, not a constant.** The
   expected size is the `bytes` value `manifest.json` records for that exact
   path, read from the bundle under test with the bundled `node` (the way the
   script already reads JSON at `:64-67`). Two reasons, both load-bearing. The
   manifest is P3.1's record of the bundle and is already inside the folder
   being tested, so this invents nothing. A hard-coded floor **would** be a new
   threshold, and HS-7 forbids inventing one inside a card; the review's
   169523 bytes is one measurement of one build, not a rule, and a floor under
   it would pass a half-copied bundle. The manifest's symlink convention
   (review finding 4) does not apply here: a Vite asset is a regular file, so
   its `bytes` is the file's own length.
4. **The check reads the served shell, so a bundle whose `index.html` and
   `assets/` disagree cannot pass.** Asserting against a file on disk would let
   a shell that references a script the bundle does not contain pass, which is
   the browser-side failure the card exists to move off the person.
5. **One `PASS` line, so the count is a tripwire.** The script prints
   `PASS spa-asset` once, and nothing else on the success path carries the
   `PASS ` prefix — the informational line Fixed decision 1 specifies does not
   touch the count. At this card's base the file prints **28** `PASS`
   lines; after this card it prints **29**, with the 28 pre-existing names in
   the same order and none weakened. A run that prints 28 means the check was
   never added, and that is `FAIL`, not `PASS` — the P4.5 V1 shape.
6. **Nothing about the launch changes.** Same `sandbox.mjs env` run, same
   relocation, same `env -i` launch under the bundled Node, same port from
   `APUNTA_P31_PORT`, same ownership poll before the first assertion, same rule-7
   shutdown, same missing-SQLite negative case, same exit-1-on-first-failure.
   The script still fails at the **first** failure, which is why the control
   stops at `spa-asset` and never reaches the whisper check.
7. **The card is L1 and offline.** It edits one test file, changes no
   production code, and needs no new build, no model, no vendor and no
   acquisition. It does launch a server on a dispatch port, exactly as the L1
   cards P2.2, P3.2, P4.1 and S2.1 do, so the dispatch assigns a port from 7800
   to 7889 and 7717 is never contacted. The one level it does **not** claim is
   the reason it does not run `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.sh`: that
   script is L3 because it compiles whisper, and P3.1 review finding 2 records
   that it re-fetches A06 from `github.com` on **every** run. A re-run of it
   here would be a second fetch this card has no authorisation for. If
   `build/linux-resources/` is absent, the rows are `NOT RUN` and the
   coordinator re-runs P3.1's V1 — never this card (Stop condition 3).

2. Add the one check, in the form Fixed decision 1 fixes, between `spa-body`

3. Re-run the script: **29** `PASS`, exit 0, `spa-asset` present, the 28
   existing names in their existing order. Record the count from both runs;
   the difference is the card's own evidence that the check is live.
4. Run V1, V2, then **V3 last** — V3 is the only row that touches the bundle,
   so nothing else may be looking at `build/linux-resources/web/dist/assets`

The bundle is put into the reviewer's own broken state — `web/dist/assets/` emptied, `index.html` left in place — and the row requires the new assertion to fail, which is what distinguishes a check that detects truncation from the three that do not. Expected, in order: the run reaches check 4 and prints `PASS spa-status`, `PASS spa-content-type` and `PASS spa-body` **first**, because the shell is intact and that is precisely the point; then `FAIL spa-asset`, and the detail shows the missing script answered **`200` with `text/html`** — the SPA fallback, not a `404` — so the content type is what caught it. `whisper-help` and the whole missing-SQLite negative case are **not** printed: the script exits on the first failure. Anything else — a run that reaches `FAIL spa-status`, one that prints 29 `PASS`, one that dies earlier on a port or ownership check — fails this row, because a control that fails for an unrelated reason proves nothing. Then the folder is restored, and **the restore proof is two assertions that can both fail.** (1) The **file count**: the row records `before-files=$n` from a non-empty before-list *before* the `mv` and refuses to go on when `n` is `0` (a bundle that was already empty is a stop, not a control), then re-counts after the restore and fails unless the count equals `n` — `restored-files=$m expected=$n`. (2) The **content**: `sha256sum -c` on that non-empty list must print `OK` for every one of the `n` files, so the bundle is byte-identical to what V1 tested. There is deliberately no `git diff --name-only` clause here: `build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:55`) and untracked, so `git diff` cannot see it and could not fail — the count and the checksums are the assertions. If the restore cannot be shown clean, that is a `FAIL` of this row and a report, not a repair. **Interruption and recovery:** the destructive span is wrapped in `restore()` under `trap restore EXIT INT TERM`, and the row prints the aside path (`aside=$c/assets-aside before-files=$n`) **before** the `mv`; that line, and `$c` itself, go in the return file. So an interrupted run — a reclaimed container, a Ctrl-C, a reboot — leaves the only copy at a path the return file names, and the fix is the one line the row prints on its own guard: `rm -rf $b/assets; mv $c/assets-aside $b/assets`. A **resumed** run must not re-enter the mutation blind, so the first thing the row does is refuse if `$c/assets-aside` already exists (a prior aside) or if `$b/assets` is missing (the interrupted case), each naming the recovery command. It never `rm -rf "$c"` over a live aside, and it never rebuilds — the recovery is a `mv` back, not a P3.1 re-run with its fresh A06 fetch (Stop condition 3) |

## Why this is a new card, and not an amendment

Recorded so the next reader does not repeat the review's own detour.

- **Not an amendment to P3.1.** Only P3.1's May edit grants
  `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.test.sh` (`P3.1.md:40`), and P3.1 is
  `APPROVED` (`docs/v2/state/PROGRESS.json:35`). An amendment to an approved
  card is not a thing the coordinator can do; a new card is.
- **Not P3.5**, though the review suggested it (`P3.1-impl.md:63-64`).
  P3.5 is WebKitGTK dictation and its May edit is `src-tauri/**`,
  `e2e/fixtures/audio-en/`, `scripts/v2/make-en-audio.sh` and
  `scripts/v2/tauri-audio.test.mjs` (`P3.5.md:22-26`). It cannot open this file,
  and a card about audio is the wrong home for a bundle-layout assertion.
- **Not P6.1**, the review's other suggestion. P6.1 is the macOS and Windows
  bundlers; its May edit names `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.sh` — the
  **packaging** script, not the test — alongside `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`,
  `Info.plist`, two new per-target scripts and a header comment
  (`P6.1.md:21-25`). It cannot open this file either, and it ships after P5.R,
  long after the Linux install path needs the check.
- So: a new card, P3.7, depending on P3.1, and a dependency of **P3.6** and
  **P3.R** — P3.R's `Depends` is generated from the child list, so P3.7 is
  picked up there automatically, and `docs/v2/DEPENDENCIES.md` is regenerated by
  `docs/v2/tools/check-plan.mjs` rather than hand-edited. The gap is closed before the
  AppImage ships and before the parent review.

## Stop conditions
1. **The check cannot be made to fail on the truncated bundle** — `spa-asset`
   passes with `web/dist/assets/` emptied. Stop and report. A green check that
   cannot fail is worse than no check, and that is the defect this card is
   about.
2. **The served `GET /` body names no `src="`, or more than one.** Report the
   count and stop; do not fall back to a `modulepreload` link, a hard-coded
   asset name, a glob over `web/dist`, or a file read from disk. This card
   asserts the shell and the server agree about one script, and a fallback
   quietly turns that into a guess.
3. **`build/linux-resources/` is absent, or `manifest.json` does not list the
   referenced path.** Both are `NOT RUN` for V1 and V3, and the coordinator
   re-runs P3.1's V1. Do not run `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.sh` from
   this card: it is L3 work and it re-fetches A06 (review finding 2).
4. **`server/src/app.ts` looks like it needs changing.** It does not, and
   changing it is a product-behaviour change outside May edit. Report the
   reason and stop (HS-9).
5. **The fix needs a hard-coded size floor, a new manifest key, a new check in
   `package-linux-resources.sh`, or anything in `web/`.** Report it as a
   finding for the coordinator and change nothing. This card adds one
   assertion to one test file; a new threshold is HS-7 territory and a
   production change is a different card.
6. **V1, V2 or V3 fails in a file outside May edit** — including a prettier or
   ESLint failure on another session's in-flight file. Report it and re-run
   later; do not reformat or fix anything outside May edit. The card's own
   required outputs are the one exception, because they are not May edit and
   `prettier --check .` covers them: a red check **on**
   `docs/v2/state/returns/P3.7.md` or anything under `docs/v2/evidence/P3.7/`
   is fixed with
   `npx prettier --write docs/v2/state/returns/P3.7.md docs/v2/evidence/P3.7/`
   and the row re-run, never reported as a stop. Every other file is the stop.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port <p> -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port <p>` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

Nothing outside this file may be downloaded, installed or pulled (HS-3).
When an item is acquired, the acquiring card records in its evidence: exact
version or revision, URL, size, SHA-256 (or the package manager's integrity
string), licence evidence, and date. The **selection rule** in each row is
fixed; a worker applies it, never replaces it.

## 1. Items

| A15 | `prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf`, the single file `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf` and nothing else in the repository | `huggingface.co` (prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf) | Hugging Face CDN hosts, on A07's terms | A07's | no | none (measurement only) |
| A16 | `Fraunces[SOFT,WONK,opsz,wght].ttf` from `github.com/google/fonts` at `ofl/fraunces`, SHA-256 `177ff6c0f14e5550a3c624247cd1189611d4eb65d000b14944c63d967958abbb`, plus its OFL 1.1 text. **Committed to the repo** beside Kalam's, used only to generate the wordmark and A outlines | `github.com` (one fetch, then never again) | `raw.githubusercontent.com` | none | no — outlines only, no font file in the bundle | P2.1 (owner amendment 2026-09-27) |

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
